correctness.rationale: All-node theorem reduces by explicit Möbius Loewner congruence to nodes in (0,1/100). Exact symbolic rational polynomial divisions prove the two-node determinant positive, the original 3-node determinant negative, and the squared 3-node determinant and all principal minors positive; continuity covers repetitions. These algebraic facts and the finite-order Loewner criterion prove the claim. Every critical identity is recomputed by the provided standalone script, with no unbounded enumeration or finite-sample leap.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The source does not imply the new converse failure, since its counterexample also violates the squared necessary test. Conversely this construction does not imply failure of the source’s full radial-convexity conjecture: the squared test may hold while higher-order global metric inequalities fail.

value.rationale: The construction is a substantive structural obstruction at the first unresolved matrix size of the motivating 2026 work: the everywhere-in-the-domain Frobenius differential necessary test alone cannot force matrix monotonicity. An exact rational analytic function and reproducible uniform coefficient certificate establish a quantified global counterexample rather than an arbitrary finite matrix or a tiny numerical improvement. The full radial-convexity question is explicitly left open.
